content: Protector Amitābha of the realm of Sukhāvatī,Look upon me with your deep blue eyes of love.Show me your moon-like face, joyful and smiling,Bestow upon me the feast of the nectar of blessings.When the end of life approaches and the breath is about to cease,May you, adorned with the major and minor marks, appear before me,And having manifested in person, may you say to me,"Do not cling to this life, come to my realm."When the channels of my body relax and grime gathers on my teeth,And experiences such as a mirage-like appearance arise,When the sign of the earth element dissolving into water occurs,Do not be afraid, do not be terrified, speak to me, Amitābha.When the nose and mouth are drawn and the tongue shortens,And experiences such as a smoke-like appearance arise,When the sign of the water element dissolving into fire occurs,Show your face and grant comfort to my soul, Amitābha.When warmth, complexion, and vitality fade and vapor escapes,And experiences such as fireflies arise,When the sign of the fire element dissolving into wind occurs,Resound with the clear melody of the Dharma, Amitābha.The body scatters and dissolves, and the breath ceases,And experiences such as a lamp-like appearance arise,When the sign of the wind element dissolving into consciousness occurs,Welcome me with joy, Amitābha.At that moment, the light rays from your heart, the tips of iron hooks,Pierce deeply into the Brahma-aperture at the crown of my head,Drawing my consciousness upward through the path of the central channel,To be placed within the hollow of a lotus in Sukhāvatī.In that instant, the sense bases of the body are perfected,Assuming a form like those of the Mahāyāna lineage,I shall behold your face and receive your teachings,May I attain the irreversible awakening.Thus, by means of clear visualization, recite the name of Amitābha as much as you are able, and seal it with the Prayer of Good Actions. This was written in a concise and clear manner by Tseten Zhabdrung Jikme Rikpe Lodro, at the earnest request of the laywoman Sherab Drolma of Khorlo Nakha.
